review_notes: I read the whole file. It gives the SuccOrder and PredOrder instances on Fin n, plus API lemmas about Order.succ and Order.pred. These instances use Mathlib's own SuccOrder and PredOrder classes through SuccOrder.ofCore and PredOrder.ofCore, so they don't introduce a competing concept. I grepped Mathlib for other SuccOrder or PredOrder instances on Fin, and for other uses of the orderSucc and orderPred names. The only matches outside this file were uses of its lemmas (in Hessenberg and TransfiniteComposition) and the WithBot/WithTop lemmas. I found no duplicate instance and no parallel successor or predecessor definition on Fin. Fin.succ and Fin.castSucc are different concepts from Order.succ. I did not look for a general SuccOrder instance that could cover Fin n.
